legend: Swing is opening a pancake factory! A good pancake factory must be good at flattening things, so Swing is going to test his new equipment on 2D matrices.
Swing is given an n×n%%ZSMJ0%% matrix M%%ZSMJ1%% containing positive integers. He has q%%ZSMJ2%% queries to ask you.

For each query, he gives you four integers x1%%ZSMJ3%%, y1%%ZSMJ4%%, x2%%ZSMJ5%%, y2%%ZSMJ6%% and asks you to flatten the submatrix bounded by (x1,y1)%%ZSMJ7%% and (x2,y2)%%ZSMJ8%% into an array A%%ZSMJ9%%. Formally, A=[M(x1,y1),M(x1,y1+1),…,M(x1,y2),M(x1+1,y1),M(x1+1,y1+1),…,M(x2,y2)]%%ZSMJ10%%.

The following image depicts the flattening of a submatrix bounded by the red dotted lines. The orange arrows denote the direction that the elements of the submatrix are appended to the back of A%%ZSMJ11%%, and A%%ZSMJ12%% is shown at the bottom of the image.
Afterwards, he asks you for the value of ∑|A|i=1Ai⋅i%%ZSMJ13%% (sum of Ai⋅i%%ZSMJ14%% over all i%%ZSMJ15%%).
input: The first line contains an integer t%%ZSMJ16%% (1≤t≤103%%ZSMJ17%%) — the number of test cases.
The first line of each test contains two integers n%%ZSMJ18%% and q%%ZSMJ19%% (1≤n≤2000,1≤q≤106%%ZSMJ20%%) — the length of M%%ZSMJ21%% and the number of queries.
The following n%%ZSMJ22%% lines contain n%%ZSMJ23%% integers each, the i%%ZSMJ24%%'th of which contains M(i,1),M(i,2),…,M(i,n)%%ZSMJ25%% (1≤M(i,j)≤106%%ZSMJ26%%).
The following q%%ZSMJ27%% lines contain four integers x1%%ZSMJ28%%, y1%%ZSMJ29%%, x2%%ZSMJ30%%, and y2%%ZSMJ31%% (1≤x1≤x2≤n,1≤y1≤y2≤n%%ZSMJ32%%) — the bounds of the query.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n%%ZSMJ33%% over all test cases does not exceed 2000%%ZSMJ34%% and the sum of q%%ZSMJ35%% over all test cases does not exceed 106%%ZSMJ36%%.
output: For each test case, output the results of the q%%ZSMJ37%% queries on a new line.
note: In the second query of the first test case, A=[9,5,5,2]%%ZSMJ38%%. Therefore, the sum is 1⋅9+2⋅5+3⋅5+4⋅2=42%%ZSMJ39%%.
